name: Misner-Sharp(-Hernandez) mass function, the invariant 1 - 2m/R = g^{ab} d_aR d_bR = Gamma^2 - U^2, its evolution equations MS-r/MS-t, and the static areal-radius form dl = dr/sqrt(1 - 2m/r)

source.located: Misner C W & Sharp D H 1964, Phys. Rev. 136, B571 -- no arXiv copy exists. Read through two independent exact restatements: Hayward, 'Gravitational energy in spherical symmetry', gr-qc/9408002v2 (PRD 53, 1938): eq. (4) p. 4 (invariant definition E = (r/2)(1 - g^{-1}(dr,dr))), eq. (27) p. 12 ('1 - 2E/r = e^{-chi}(r')^2 - rdot^2, which is the form actually given by Misner & Sharp [4], with different notation'), eqs (28a,b) p. 12 (variation formulas), eqs (31)-(32b) pp. 12-13 (the comoving perfect-fluid forms MS considered), Prop. 1 p. 4 (trapping), regular centre E = O(r^3) p. 4; and Escriva, arXiv:2504.05813v3 (JCAP 2025), section 2 pp. 3-5: eqs (2.1)-(2.5), (2.9), (2.12), (2.24), which cites Misner & Sharp as [57] 'for the details of the derivation'. Hernandez & Misner 1966 (ApJ 143, 452) NAMED-NOT-READ (Escriva ref. [79]). Hochberg & Visser gr-qc/9802046v2 read at pp. 23-29 (sections 6.1-6.2, eqs 69-90; section 7 is the Discussion).

published_statement: Hayward eq. (4), G = 1: 'E = (1/2) r (1 - g^{-1}(dr,dr)) = (1/2) r + e^{f} r d_+r d_-r = (1/2) r + (1/4) e^{f} r^3 theta_+ theta_-' -- 'The form actually given by Misner & Sharp is derived in Section IV. Note that E is an invariant. Indeed, the only invariants of the metric and its first derivatives are functions of r and E'. Section IV, line-element (26) 'ds^2 = r^2 dOmega^2 + e^{chi} dxi^2 - dtau^2' with (23b) g(d/dtau, d/dtau) = -1 and (23a) orthogonality, eq. (27): '1 - 2E/r = e^{-chi}(r')^2 - rdot^2, which is the form actually given by Misner & Sharp [4], with different notation.' Variation formulas (28a,b): E' = 4 pi r^2 (T_00 r' - T_01 rdot), Edot = 4 pi r^2 e^{-chi} (T_01 r' - T_11 rdot). Misner & Sharp's own setting (31a,b): a perfect fluid T = (mu + p) dtau dtau + p g with tau the fluid proper time, giving (32a,b) E' = 4 pi r^2 mu r', Edot = -4 pi r^2 p rdot, and (33) E = INT_0^xi 4 pi r^2 mu r' dxi from a regular centre. Prop. 1: 'A metric sphere is trapped iff E > r/2, marginal iff E = r/2, untrapped iff E < r/2. Proof. By definition.' Regular centre: 'g^{-1}(dr,dr) - 1 = O(r^2) ... Then E = O(r^3) at a regular centre.' Escriva (2.2)-(2.5): metric -A^2 dt^2 + B^2 dr^2 + R^2 dOmega^2 in the comoving gauge; U = D_t R = (1/A) dR/dt, Gamma = D_r R = (1/B) dR/dr 'where D_t and D_r are the proper time and distance derivatives'; M(R) = INT_0^R 4 pi R~^2 rho dR~ (2.4); 'Gamma = sqrt(1 + U^2 - 2M/R) (2.5), where Gamma is called the generalised Lorentz factor'; D_t M = -4 pi R^2 U p (2.9); D_r M = 4 pi Gamma rho R^2 (2.12); M = (R/2)(1 + U^2 - Gamma^2) (2.24); and p. 5: 'For type-II fluctuations, solving Gamma with the constraint Eq.(2.5) would not be convenient, since Gamma takes negative values in the throat structure'.
published_hypotheses: Spherical symmetry throughout (Hayward p. 2: 'Since the whole article is concerned with spherical symmetry, this case will be assumed implicitly in the Propositions'; Escriva (2.2)); all arguments local
r is the areal radius (area 4 pi r^2); E/m is defined on spheres, not hypersurfaces (Hayward p. 17: 'the general definition (4) or (27) is a function of spheres only')

The definition (4) is purely geometric: no field equation, no energy condition, no staticity (Hayward Section II is 'purely geometrical'; the Einstein equations enter only in Section III/IV for (28), (32))
The chart form (27) needs the coordinates (23a,b): tau proper time along the slice normal, xi orthogonal -- i.e. lapse 1, zero shift (the tree's Phi = 0 gauge)

Misner & Sharp's own 1964 form: adiabatic perfect fluid (31a), comoving coordinates tau = fluid proper time (Hayward p. 12; Escriva p. 3: 'the Einstein field equations written in the comoving slicing and comoving threading'), G = c = 1
The integral form E = INT 4 pi r^2 mu r' dxi (Hayward (33); Escriva (2.4)) needs a REGULAR CENTRE E(0) = 0 (Hayward: 'if Sigma has a regular centre xi = 0, (32a) integrates to (33)')
Positivity E >= 0 (Hayward Prop. 6) needs the DOMINANT energy condition AND an untrapped hypersurface AND a regular centre; 'E may be negative, as in the negative-energy Schwarzschild solution'
Escriva (2.5) as written takes the positive square root; Escriva himself notes Gamma < 0 occurs (type-II) and evolves Gamma by (2.21) instead
hypothesis_drift: certify.py:113-116 ADDS an unwritten hypothesis: 'Every static spherically symmetric spacetime can be written with an areal radius ... dr^2/(1 - 2m(r)/r)' requires the areal radius to be a good coordinate (dR/dl != 0, no extremal sphere) and 1 - 2m/r > 0. Hayward's definition (4) needs neither. At a throat r' = 0 the areal chart is singular while the gauge-free definition gives m = r_0/2 > 0 and no contraction (rederivation C4, C7, z3 G4) -- so the theorem's VERDICT is unaffected; the drift is in the word 'every'. The tree's own throatmass.py:19-23 and nonstatic.py:28-30 already use the gauge-free form. Also: 'untrapped' is not an extra hypothesis on the static slice -- z3 G3 shows U = 0 => 1 - 2m/R = W^2 >= 0.

later_literature.what: The invariant form (4), Prop. 1 (trapping by E/r), monotonicity (Prop. 5, DEC, untrapped), positivity (Prop. 6, DEC + untrapped + regular centre), Kodama charge (App. B), ADM/Bondi limits; states E 'may be negative, as in the negative-energy Schwarzschild solution' and 'Even the Schwarzschild energy may be negative'. Everything the tree uses is here unchanged.

Generalised Misner-Sharp mass m = ... r^{n-3}[k - (Dr)^2] ... (2.7) 'reduces to the Misner-Sharp quasi-local mass' in 4D GR; variation formulas (2.18)-(2.19) 'exactly the same as those in general relativity'. p. 9: 'In the positivity proof of the Misner-Sharp mass (n = 4, k = 1, Lambda = 0) in [10] (= Hayward gr-qc/9408002), it is claimed that Proposition 5 follows immediately from Proposition 4 together with the fact that a regular center is surrounded by untrapped surfaces ... However, because the sign of m around the regular center depends on the value of C as seen in Lemma 1, the positivity of m around the regular center seems to be nontrivial, which requires Lemma 2 for completion of the proof.' This narrows Hayward's PROOF of positivity (a downstream proposition under DEC), not the definition or the identity; the tree does not rest on Prop. 6 (specthm facts_outside D4 records RESTS=False on the positive-energy theorem). Also p. 1: the Brown-York mass 'does not reproduce the Misner-Sharp mass in the spherically symmetric case. Thus, the uniqueness of the mass function in condition (iv) is still an open problem'.

Misner-Sharp formalism carried into the type-II regime where R is non-monotonic and Gamma < 0; (2.5)'s square root is explicitly not used to solve Gamma there; 'when Gamma < 0, the integrand in Eq. (2.4) ... includes a locally negative mass component within that radius' (p. 12). Confirms the identity (2.24) and the tree's squared-form use; shows the sqrt branch of (2.5) is a hypothesis.

Section 6.2, metric (84) with mass function m(v,r): theta_+ = 0 <=> 2m(r,v) = r (marginal sphere at 2m = r, Hayward Prop. 1 in another chart); flare-out at the throat <=> T_vv <= 0 (NEC violated or marginal). Cited by the tree as 's7'; the content is in section 6.

lacked_data: M's hypothesis tested. What Misner & Sharp had in 1964: the Einstein equations, a perfect fluid, comoving coordinates, and the Schwarzschild exterior. What came after: Hernandez-Misner observer-time coordinates (1966); Cahill-McVittie's and Hayward's invariant form (1970/1994); Kodama's conserved current (1980) and its identification with E (Hayward App. B); the trapping-horizon framework and Prop. 1; the ADM/Bondi limit identifications; the positive-energy theorems (Schoen-Yau 1979, Witten 1981) and their spherical form Prop. 6; the Maeda-Nozawa 2008 correction to Hayward's positivity proof; the type-II (Gamma < 0) collapse regime (Escriva 2025); quantum-inequality results on negative energy; the 2025 instability of negative-mass stars. Evidence that none of it moves this result: the object is a DEFINITION plus an algebraic IDENTITY in the metric functions and contains no measured datum (rederivation A0-A6, F1, G2-G9 hold with no physical input); every later source read restates the same definition and identity verbatim and builds on it (Hayward (4)/(27); Escriva (2.24); Maeda-Nozawa (2.7) at alpha = 0, Lambda = 0, n = 4, k = 1 with 'variation formulae exactly the same as those in general relativity'). Evidence that later data DID narrow something nearby: (i) Maeda-Nozawa show Hayward's positivity proof needed a lemma he did not supply -- a gap in a DEC-dependent downstream proposition the tree does not rest on; (ii) Escriva shows the positive square root in (2.5) is a physical restriction, not a theorem -- the tree's squared-form use is unaffected. So for THIS result the answer to M's question is: the 1964 authors lacked much, and none of it bears on a definition; what it bears on is the positivity and sign claims built on top of the definition, which the board already refuses to assume (it takes m < 0 as its demand, not as forbidden).

(4)/(27)/(28); Escriva (2.3)-(2.5), (2.9), (2.12), (2.24)), and the re-derivation from the Christoffel symbols reproduces every form the tree states with residual exactly 0 (37/37, exit 0). No numerical datum enters. The recorded drifts are (a) certify.py:113's 'every static spherically symmetric spacetime can be written [in areal form]' -- an unwritten regularity of the areal chart, harmless to the verdict because the gauge-free definition the rest of the tree uses gives m = r_0/2 > 0 and no contraction at the excluded points (C7, G4), and 'untrapped' is a consequence of U = 0 (G3); (b) attribution: the invariant form is Hayward's presentation and the flux-bearing MS-r/MS-t are Hayward (28a,b), reducing to Misner-Sharp's fluid forms at j = 0 (B5-B6); (c) Escriva (2.5)'s sqrt is a branch the tree does not use; (d) the 'Hochberg & Visser s7' citation names the Discussion where the content is section 6. None is a refutation, none is a narrowing of the class the board's verdicts range over; all are recorded, nothing repaired. Misner & Sharp 1964 itself remains NAMED-NOT-READ; the grade rests on two independent restatements that agree with each other and with the machine check.
